chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, from Ṣāliḥ ibn ʿUqbah, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad al-Jaʿfarī, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام; and from ʿUqbah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed Allah created the creatures, so He created what He loved from among what He loved, and what He loved to create, He created from the clay of Paradise. And He created what He hated from among what He hated, and what He hated to create, He created from the clay of the Fire. Then He sent them forth in the shadows.

So I said, 'And what are the shadows?' He said, 'Have you not seen your shadow in the sun? It is a thing, yet it is not a thing.' Then Allah sent the Prophets among them, calling them to acknowledge Allah, and this is His saying:
And if you ask them who created them, they will surely say: Allah.

Then He called them to acknowledge the Prophets, so some of them acknowledged and some denied. Then He called them to our wilayah, so by Allah, the one who acknowledged it was the one whom He loved, and the one who denied it was the one whom He hated. And this is His saying:
So they were not going to believe in what they had denied before.
Then Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: 'The denial was there.'

key_terms.التَّكْذِيبُ: denial or belying that occurred previously
key_terms.الظِّلَالِ: the shadows, a subtle prior state in which the creatures were sent forth
key_terms.النَّبِيِّينَ: the Prophets sent by Allah to call creation
key_terms.الْخَلْقَ: the created beings or creatures brought into existence by Allah
key_terms.طِينَةِ النَّارِ: the clay of the Fire, describing the origin of those whom Allah hated
key_terms.طِينَةِ الْجَنَّةِ: the clay of Paradise, describing the origin of those whom Allah loved
key_terms.وَلَايَتِنَا: our wilayah, referring to the divinely appointed authority of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain the primordial acknowledgment of Allah, the Prophets, and the wilayah of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a theological account of creation, primordial testing, and the recognition of Allah, the Prophets, and the wilayah of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام. It connects this pre-temporal acknowledgement and denial to Quranic language, explaining later belief and rejection as rooted in an earlier reality. The report is significant in Shia thought for its strong linkage between tawhid, prophethood, and wilayah.
